suggested_english: {REL} has swollen legs and cannot breathe well when lying flat
suggestion_note: gloss 'swollen legs and breathless lying flat'. THIRD PERSON ONLY — the first is held on ONE Kinyarwanda word, 'ngaramye', which is what makes the phrase orthopnoea rather than ordinary breathlessness. That hold does not transfer as a wording question, because English says 'lying flat' without difficulty; but the row it protects is the first person and the speaker's own third is accepted and needs none of those forms. Matches '{REL} yabyimbye ibirenge kandi ntashobora guhumeka neza iyo aryamye agaramye.' 'When lying flat' carries the agaramye sense that the concept depends on.
